items.prompt: Black to move. The queen and bishop line up against f7. Black is already in trouble: which move limits the damage?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...Rc8.
...Nb6 is worse than ...Rc8 by at least 40 centipawns.
The white queen attacks f7, with the bishop behind her.

hints: Black cannot easily guard f7 twice. What else can the rook do?
The black queen is on c2; which file is open to her friend?
A rook move to the open file.
items.explain: The rook comes to the open c-file next to the queen, so that the queen can take on c1 with check and the rooks can trade. That limits the damage; moves that try to guard f7 directly lose more. At depth 16 ...Rc8 is the engine's first choice and ...Nb6 is clearly behind.

feedback_by_move.d7b6: Guards nothing important and allows Qxf7+ lines; the engine rates it clearly behind ...Rc8.
feedback_by_move.f8e7: Does not meet the threat: the engine rates it much worse.

items.prompt: Black to move. The b2 pawn is attacked and nothing protects it. Should the queen take?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...Qxb2.
...Nc6 is worse than ...Qxb2 by at least 30 centipawns.
The black queen attacks b2.

hints: Where can the queen go after the capture?
White's rook will attack her. Is there a square where she is safe and still annoying?
The queen takes the pawn.
items.explain: The queen takes the pawn, and after Rb1 she goes to a3 where nothing attacks her. White gets time for an attack but Black has no direct danger. At depth 16 the capture is the engine's first choice; developing moves are behind.

feedback_by_move.b8c6: Develops, but gives up the pawn offer: the engine rates it behind taking.

items.prompt: An edited position (not from a game): Black's a-pawn stands on a5 instead of a6. Black to move, king and rooks at home. Is the queen grab ...Qxc2 a good move?

claims.statement: ...Qxc2 scores at least 90 cp worse than the top move (depth 16).
A black pawn stands on a5.

hints: Does the a-pawn have anything to do with the queen grab?
Count what White's queen on d5 already attacks.
No: the grab is still bad.
items.explain: The a-pawn is on the other wing and has nothing to do with the grab: the king and rooks are still at home and f7 faces a queen with a bishop coming. The engine still rates ...Qxc2 clearly behind ...Be7.

options: yes
no

items.prompt: Black to move. White's queen has just taken a knight on d5, and Black's king and both rooks are still at home. Is the queen grab ...Qxc2 a good move?

claims.statement: ...Qxc2 is worse than ...Be7 by at least 90 centipawns.
After ...Qxc2 and Bc4 the white queen attacks f7, with the bishop behind her.

hints: Before taking, count what White's queen on d5 already attacks.
What happens to the pawn on f7 once White's bishop comes to c4?
No: the king is still in the centre.
items.explain: The queen takes the pawn but leaves the king and the f7 pawn facing a queen with a bishop behind her. Developing the bishop or a rook keeps the position level. At depth 16 ...Be7 and ...Rc8 are close to the best and ...Qxc2 is clearly worse.

options: yes
no

items.prompt: Black to move. White has opened the f-pawn and Black's pieces are asleep. Which move is best?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...Be7 or ...Nc6.
...h6 is worse than ...Be7 by at least 100 centipawns.
...d5 is worse than ...Be7 by at least 100 centipawns.

hints: Count the black pieces that have not moved. How many are asleep?
A pawn move asks White a question but develops nothing. What might White answer?
A piece move that gets the king nearer to castling.
items.explain: The bishop to e7 develops, prepares castling and meets fxe6 with a recapture. The pawn moves ...h6 and ...d5 each develop nothing and give White a free tempo with open lines in front of the king. At depth 16 ...Be7 and ...Nc6 are close to the best; ...h6 and ...d5 each lose about a pawn and a half.

feedback_by_move.h7h6: It asks the bishop a question, but Bxf6 gxf6 fxe6 fxe6 Bc4 comes with open lines; the engine rates it far behind.
feedback_by_move.d6d5: Opens the centre while Black is behind in development; the engine rates it far behind.
feedback_by_move.e6e5: Blocks the knight but weakens d5; the engine rates it behind.

items.prompt: Black to move. White threatens g5 and a jump to d5. Which move starts the counterplay?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...b4.
...Ne8 is worse than ...b4 by at least 100 centipawns.
...h5 is worse than ...b4 by at least 100 centipawns.
After ...b4 a black pawn attacks the knight on c3.

hints: In a race the side that spends a move on defence usually loses it. Which Black pawn can attack White's king's wing?
The knight on c3 guards d5. What would attack it?
A pawn move that hits the knight.
items.explain: The b-pawn attacks the knight on c3, which guards d5, so the pawn lever both gains time and challenges White's best square. Passive moves like ...Ne8 and ...h5 start no counterplay and let White play h4 and Nd5 at leisure. At depth 16 ...b4 is the engine's first choice; ...Ne8 and ...h5 each lose more than a pawn and a half.

feedback_by_move.f6e8: Retreats and starts nothing: White plays h4 and Nd5 and the engine rates it clearly worse for Black.
feedback_by_move.h7h5: A flank move that ignores the b-pawn lever; the engine rates it clearly behind ...b4.
feedback_by_move.a6a5: Hangs the pawn on b5 to Bxb5.

items.prompt: White to move. The bishop on c5 attacks the knight on d4, which stands in front of the queen. Which move keeps White in the game?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Bg3.
O-O (the game move) is worse than Bg3 by at least 150 centipawns.
Two black pieces (the bishop on c5 and the queen on e5) attack the knight on d4.

hints: Count what is on the diagonal from c5: which White pieces line up?
The knight on d4 is pinned to the queen on e3. A black move will attack it again. Which white move hits the black queen first?
The bishop retreats with an attack on the queen on e5.
items.explain: The bishop on c5 pins the knight on d4 to the queen on e3. Bg3 attacks the black queen first, gaining a tempo before the pin bites. Castling ignores the pin: Black plays ...Nc6 and adds a second attacker to the pinned knight. At depth 16 Bg3 is the engine's first choice and castling loses more than two pawns.

feedback_by_move.e1g1: The game move: it ignores the pin, and after ...Nc6 the engine rates the position more than two pawns better for Black.

items.prompt: White to move after 17...Nc6. The knight on d4 is pinned and attacked twice. White is worse, so which move is the best defence?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers c3.
Rxf7 is worse than c3 by at least 150 centipawns.
Bc4 is worse than c3 by at least 150 centipawns.

hints: Count the attackers and defenders of the knight on d4.
A desperate sacrifice rarely saves a worse position. What quiet move adds a defender?
A pawn move that protects d4.
items.explain: The pawn move to c3 adds a second defender to the knight on d4, so the pin stops winning material at once. White stays worse, but the sacrifices Rxf7 and Bc4 give up material for nothing. At depth 16 c3 is the engine's first choice and both desperados lose at least a pawn and a half more.

feedback_by_move.f1f7: A desperado: the engine rates it much worse than c3.
feedback_by_move.e2c4: Gives up the bishop for nothing; the engine rates it much worse.

items.prompt: White to move. The black knight attacks the bishop on e3, and the black knight on f6 stands in front of the e5 square. What does White play?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers e5.
Bd4 (the game move) is worse than e5 by at least 100 centipawns.
After e5 the pawn attacks the knight on f6.

hints: Counter-attack first: can White hit a black piece with tempo?
The pawn on e4 can advance and attack the knight on f6.
A pawn move to e5.
items.explain: The pawn jumps to e5 and attacks the knight on f6, so Black cannot simply take on e3 without losing time. If Black takes, the recapture opens the f-file, and White's pieces come alive. In the game White retreated with Bd4. Bd4 is 0.6 to 1.6 pawns behind e5 depending on the search, yet it still keeps a small White edge; the game was lost later. A result is not an evaluation.

feedback_by_move.e3d4: The game move: it moves the bishop out of the attack but gives the initiative away; the engine rates it 0.6 to 1.6 pawns behind e5 (still a small White edge).
feedback_by_move.e3c5: The engine rates it much worse than e5.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's knight on b3 and pawn on g5 press. Which move holds on best?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...Ne5 or ...Nb6.
...Bxb3 (the game move) is worse by at least 80 centipawns.

hints: Trading a defender helps the attacker. Which black piece protects the king?
A knight move can keep the pieces together and still cover key squares.
The knight on d7 has two good squares.
items.explain: Moving the knight keeps the light-square bishop. A trade on b3 with ...Bxb3 cxb3 would give Black's rook the c-file against the king on b1, but it costs about a pawn and Black is already worse. At depth 16 ...Ne5 and ...Nb6 are close to the best.

feedback_by_move.e6b3: The game move: it trades off a defender and opens the c-file for the white king's attackers; the engine rates it clearly behind.

items.prompt: Black to move after 10.Be2. Which developing move is best?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...Nbd7.
...Nc6 (the game move) is worse than ...Nbd7 by at least 40 centipawns.

hints: Where will the knight be exchanged? Which square leaves the other pieces free?
The knight on c6 can be traded by Nxc6 and damage the pawns.
The b8 knight can go to d7.
items.explain: The knight to d7 keeps the pawn structure healthy and leaves c6 free for a later bishop move. The game move ...Nc6 allowed a trade that doubled Black's pawns. At depth 16 ...Nbd7 is the engine's first choice and ...Nc6 trails it.

feedback_by_move.b8c6: The game move: it allowed Nxc6 bxc6 with a damaged pawn structure; the engine rates it behind ...Nbd7.
